project.title: Anion Exchange Chromatography-Based Purification of Exosomes from Brassica oleracea L.
project.projectDescription: A purification platform that integrates ultrafiltration (UF) with anion exchange chromatography in a fast protein liquid chromatography (FPLC) system, which provides superior resolution, reproducibility, and automation, making it an ideal choice for scaling up exosome isolation.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Pooled samples of anion exchange-FPLC purified B. oleracea exosomes, corresponding to 0.7 mg of proteins, were dried in SpeedVac roto-evaporator (ThermoFisher Scientific, USA); the pellet was extracted using 50 μL of lysis buffer containing 7 M urea, 2 M thiourea, 4% w/v 3-[(3-cholamidopropyl)dimethylammonio]-1-propanesulfonate e 1% w/v dithiothreitol, and added with a protease inhibitor cocktail for plant tissues (Merck-Sigma-Aldrich, Darmstadt, Germany). The sample was sonicated in an ultrasonication bath three times for 4 min, with 2 min between bursts and left in ice for 1 h. After lysis, the sample was centrifuged at 16,000 x g for 10 min, at 4 °C, and the supernatant was collected. The protein concentration was determined using the Quick Start TM Bradford Protein Assay and 500 g of the sample was analysed in triplicate with preparative 12% T SDS-PAGE under reducing conditions. For protein identification, above-reported preparative SDS-PAGE gels were cut into 24 parallel slices, which were triturated, washed with water and acetonitrile, S-alkylated with 55 mM iodoacetamide in 100 mM NH4HCO3, washed again, and finally digested with trypsin (12.5 ng/µL in 50 mM NH4HCO3, 5 mM CaCl2). The resulting peptide mixtures were desalted/concentrated using ZipTip C18 (Merck), vacuum-dried in a Savant roto-evaporator (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and finally reconstituted in 0.1% v/v formic acid prior to MS analysis. A duplicate experiment was accomplished. Peptide mixtures were analyzed by means of a nanoLC-ESI-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS platform consisting of an UltiMate 3000 HPLC RSLC nano-chromatography system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany) linked to a Q-ExactivePlus mass spectrometer through a Nanoflex ion source (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany).
project.dataProcessingProtocol: For protein identification, all raw mass data files associated with protein digests of slices were merged in a unique file that was subjected to analysis with Proteome Discoverer v. 2.4 software (Thermo Fisher Scientific), enabling database search with Mascot algorithm v. 2.4.2 (Matrix Science) according to a shotgun proteomic approach. Database searching was performed using a B. oleracea L. protein sequence database downloaded from UniProtKB (121,712 entries, 01/2024)
